drills.title: An RGB color record
hints: Structure Color with three Nat fields red, green, blue, deriving Repr.
Define yellow by applying Color's default constructor to 255, 255, 0.
Evaluate the projection Color.red, applied as an ordinary function to yellow.

drills.title: Dependent pairs as an inductive type
hints: Inductive type Sigma with an implicit parameter α : Type u and an explicit parameter β : α → Type v.
Its single constructor mk, with its type written out as a dependent arrow: given a : α and an element of β a, it produces Sigma β.

drills.title: Countably branching trees
hints: Inductive type CBTree with two constructors: leaf, and sup, which takes a function from Nat to CBTree.
Open the namespace CBTree.
Define succ of t : CBTree as sup applied to the constant function returning t, ignoring its argument.
Define toCBTree : Nat → CBTree by equations: 0 goes to leaf, and n+1 goes to succ of toCBTree n.
Define omega : CBTree as sup applied to toCBTree.
Close the namespace.

drills.title: Zero is a left identity, by induction
hints: Theorem zero_add: for n : Nat, 0 + n = n, in tactic mode.
Induct on n, giving the cases as named alternatives attached directly to the induction tactic.
zero alternative: close by rfl.
succ alternative, naming the predecessor n and the induction hypothesis ih: rewrite with Nat.add_succ and then ih.

drills.title: Zero is a left identity, case by case
hints: Theorem zero_add: for n : Nat, 0 + n = n, in tactic mode.
Induct on n, with nothing attached to the induction tactic.
Address the zero goal by its tag and close it by rfl.
Address the succ goal by its tag, naming the predecessor n and the induction hypothesis ih; rewrite with Nat.add_succ and then ih.

drills.title: Remainder is below the divisor
hints: Anonymous example: for x : Nat, implicit y : Nat, and h : y > 0, prove x % y < y, in tactic mode.
Induct on x and y together using the custom induction principle Nat.mod.inductionOn, with named alternatives attached to the tactic.
ind alternative, binding x, y, h₁, ih: rewrite with Nat.mod_eq_sub_mod applied to the second component of h₁.
Then close it exactly with ih applied to h.
base alternative, binding x, y, h₁: have an unnamed fact ¬ 0 < y ∨ ¬ y ≤ x, given by Iff.mp of Decidable.not_and_iff_or_not (eliding all its explicit arguments at once), applied to h₁.
Pattern-match on that unnamed fact.
Left case, naming its hypothesis h₁: close exactly with absurd applied to h and h₁.
Right case, also naming its hypothesis h₁: have hgt : y > x from Nat.gt_of_not_le h₁.
Rewrite inside hgt, right to left, with Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hgt (turning it into y > x % y).
Close the goal with the assumption tactic.

drills.title: Destructuring in intro and funext
hints: Anonymous example in tactic mode: s ∧ q ∧ r → p ∧ r → q ∧ p (with p, q, r, s auto-bound).
Introduce both hypotheses, destructuring them in the intro itself: from the first keep only the proof hq of q, ignoring the rest; from the second keep only hp, ignoring the rest.
Close the goal exactly with the pair built directly from hq and hp.

Second anonymous example in tactic mode: the function of x, y : Nat × Nat returning x's first component plus y's second equals the function of x, z : Nat × Nat returning z's second component plus x's first.
Apply function extensionality, destructuring the first argument into a and b and the second into c and d.
Restate the goal as a + d = d + a.
Rewrite with Nat.add_comm.

drills.title: Successor is injective
hints: Open the Nat namespace.
Anonymous example: for m n k : Nat and h : succ (succ m) = succ (succ n), prove n + k = m + k, in tactic mode.
Use injection on h, naming the resulting equation h'.
Use injection on h', naming the resulting equation h''.
Rewrite with h''.

drills.title: Closing goals from constructor clashes
hints: Open the Nat namespace.
Anonymous example: for m n : Nat and h : succ m = 0, prove n = n + 7, in tactic mode, using only injection on h.
The same example again, this time closed by the contradiction tactic.
Anonymous example: from h : 7 = 4 prove False, by the contradiction tactic.

drills.title: Mutually inductive even and odd
hints: Open a block of mutually defined inductive types.
Even : Nat → Prop, with constructors even_zero proving Even 0, and even_succ taking a named n : Nat and a proof of Odd n to give Even (n + 1).
Odd : Nat → Prop, with one constructor odd_succ taking a named n : Nat and a proof of Even n to give Odd (n + 1).
Close the block.
